chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him about eating the lizard (dabb). So he said: 'Indeed the lizard, the mouse, the monkeys, and the pigs are transformed creatures (musukh).'

key_terms.الضَّبّ: Dabb — a large, spiny-tailed lizard native to the Arabian and Saharan deserts, considered haram to eat in the Shia tradition
key_terms.مُسُوخ: Musukh (plural of maskh) — transformed/morphed creatures; beings whose outward form was changed from their original human or other form as divine punishment

ai.seo_question: Why is eating dabb (desert lizard) forbidden in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) declares that four animals — the dabb (desert lizard), the mouse, the monkey, and the pig — are musukh: creatures whose current form is the result of divine transformation as a punishment for human sin. This theological-jurisprudential ruling reinforces the prohibition on consuming these animals and links it to their nature as transformed beings. In classical Islamic tradition, musukh refers to groups of humans who were cursed and transformed into animals due to disobedience, making their consumption both legally forbidden and spiritually reprehensible.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘
I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about eating the lizard. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The lizard, and the mouse, and the monkey, and the pigs, are morphed (creatures)’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabiy who has said the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam,
about eating lizards. He (the Imam) said, ‘Lizards, rats, apes and pigs are metamorphosed.’”
